analysis.investment_thesis: GMR Power & Urban Infra sits in the infrastructure/utility space — explicitly excluded from my Magic Formula universe — with an earnings yield of ~8.5% and ROCE of just 13.2%, both well below my minimum thresholds. The business barely covers its interest expense (Finance Cost ₹1,571 Cr vs. Operating Income ₹1,534 Cr), making reported profits entirely dependent on volatile "Other Income."
key_strengths: Strong OCF trajectory: operating cash flow grew from ₹588 Cr (2021) to ₹2,833 Cr (2025), 5/5 years positive
Revenue CAGR of 23.4% over 4 years signals real business scale-up
Low capex intensity (₹270 Cr capex vs. ₹2,833 Cr OCF in FY25) — good FCF conversion at the operating level
key_risks: Interest coverage is essentially zero: Finance Cost (₹1,571 Cr) nearly equals Operating Income (₹1,534 Cr) — one bad year destroys solvency
Net profit is illusory — ₹1,552 Cr profit in FY25 driven by ₹2,228 Cr 'Other Income'; operating profit alone cannot service debt
Equity was negative for four consecutive years (2021–2024), turning positive only in FY25; D/E of 7.31 reflects extreme balance sheet fragility
red_flags: Infrastructure/utility company — excluded from Magic Formula universe by design
Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) ~8.5%: EBIT ₹1,534 Cr / EV ~₹18,151 Cr — below my 12% minimum
ROCE of 13.2% is well below the 20% threshold for a 'good business'
Net profit swings wildly: -₹2,185 Cr → -₹652 Cr → +₹1,139 Cr → -₹127 Cr → +₹1,552 Cr — driven by non-operational items, not durable earnings
ROE of 110.2% is a statistical artifact of a near-zero equity base — not genuine capital efficiency
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math disqualifies this immediately on two fronts. First, infrastructure/utility companies are excluded from my universe because heavy leverage distorts both metrics. Second, even ignoring that exclusion: Earnings Yield = EBIT ₹1,534 Cr / EV ~₹18,151 Cr (Market Cap ₹8,590 Cr + Debt ₹10,250 Cr - Cash ₹689 Cr) = ~8.5% — below my 12% floor. ROCE of 13.2% is similarly below my 20% threshold for a business worth owning. Both Magic Formula legs fail simultaneously.

The balance sheet tells an even grimmer story. Finance costs of ₹1,571 Cr in FY25 consume essentially all of the ₹1,534 Cr operating income, meaning the business cannot service its debt from operations alone. The ₹1,552 Cr net profit is a mirage — strip out the ₹2,228 Cr "Other Income" and the company loses money operationally. With ₹10,250 Cr of debt against ₹1,408 Cr of freshly-turned-positive equity, one adverse year in "Other Income" (asset sales, one-time gains) erases the equity cushion entirely. The operating cash flow improvement is encouraging but insufficient to change the fundamental picture of a heavily indebted infrastructure vehicle earning subpar returns on capital.
